5 Expert Tips On Cleaning Stained Tile and Grout

December 03, 2022

Tiles are the most noticeable element of every home. They can become a centerpiece in your kitchen and bathroom if they are well-maintained. As beautiful as it looks, it takes a good cleaning to keep its pristine condition. For some, hiring cleaning servicesare the way to go.

Table of Contents

Generally, it is easy to clean tiles. But tile and grout cleaningis another story. Moreover, cleaning grout is an important part of keeping your tiles looking spotless and impressive.

If you are looking for the best way to do tile and grout cleaning, keep reading. We will share with you 5 expert tips on how to deal with the dirt in your tiles and grout.

What do I need to clean my tiles and grouts?

The professional tile and grout cleaning costdoesn’t come cheap. The good thing is that, you could do it by yourself. All the things you need for cleaning are found in your home. Below are the things you’ll need:

  • Brush
  • Vinegar
  • Baking soda
  • Spray bottle
  • Hydrogen peroxide
  • Commercial grout cleaner
  • Bleach
  • Mop

5 Tips for Tile and Grout Cleaning

Now, we’re going to share with you practical tips on how you can achieve the same results when hiring a tile and grout cleaning servicenear you.

DIY steam cleaning tile floors and grout

You can buy a steam cleaner for your grout and tile cleaningtask. This device creates steam that helps penetrate through the grout for deep cleaning. Steam is hotter than boiling water, so it can effectively disinfect your tiles and grouts.

This device heats water up to 200 degrees Celsius. The vapor produced is injected into your floor upon mopping. That said, it can efficiently deep clean those dark or yellow stains on your tiles and grouts.

Daily cleaning

One of the best house cleaning tips that you should never forget is daily cleaning. Stains and dirt pile up on your floor tiles daily. To avoid having a hard time cleaning them, do that every day. That way, you are removing those stains slowly every day. Moreover, you’re preventing molds from growing on your tiles.

For your daily tile cleaning, you can make your own tile cleaner. You can mix baking soda, dishwashing soap solution, and hydrogen peroxide. Mix them all and place them inside a spray bottle. Use this solution in cleaning your tiles and grouts.

You can also use lukewarm water for cleaning your tiles. It helps soften stains and grime, so you can easily mop them out.

Reseal your grouts annually

We recommend that you reseal your grouts every year. This is necessary to continually keep stain resistance on your floors and walls. The grout keeps molds and bacteria from getting underneath your tiles and growing there.

When your grouts are replenished annually, they can better wick off moisture and stains. You can hire a professional cleaner to do that for you. You can also buy over-the-counter grout sealers if you want to do this on your own.

Alternatively, hiring a reliable tile and grout cleaning companycan help you with that concern. Our trained professionals are equipped with the proper tools and products for resealing grouts in your kitchen and bathroom.

Check if it’s time to apply a new grout

You can easily tell by visually checking your grouts if they need to be re-applied. Oftentimes, strong chemicals like dilute hydrochloric acid or strong bleach can damage your tiles and grouts. This can weaken their structure, so stains and bacteria can penetrate easily.

Alternatively, asking for assistance from a grout expert would be essential. They have the right tools and skills to effectively check and re-grout your tiles. Our professionals are your best help in this situation. Check your countertops. You don’t want dirt where you prepare your food, right? Marble countertop cleaningis also essential, and this should be taken into account if new grout needs to be applied.

Use vinegar and lukewarm water

White vinegar mixed with warm water is a common DIY tile and grout cleaner. The vinegar is a weak acid, which can gradually dissolve stains and grime on your grouts and tiles. Warm water helps soften that dirt and stains, so you can easily brush them out.

You can use a stiff-bristled brush for this matter. A steam cleaner would also be good if you have one. When preparing your house cleaning checklist, these things should never be missed!

What are the different kinds of grouts?

There are three types of grouts used in installing tiles – sanded, unsanded, and epoxy grouts. Among these types, epoxy grout has the highest resistance to water and stains. Cement-based grouts tend to absorb more moisture than epoxy.

You usually find epoxy grouts applied on your kitchen countertops and backsplash. They are typically more expensive than cement grouts. Plus, you can dye your epoxy to match its color with your tiles. They would look seamless for that matter.

When you’ll be using polished stones, between sanded and unsanded, use the unsanded grout. This contains less grit, so there’ll be less chance of scratching your glossy tiles. Sanded grouts, on the other hand, are good for larger joints. They are good for high-traffic areas, like your kitchen and bathroom floors.

Does oxygen bleach work for cleaning tiles and grouts?

Definitely, this one works for tough stains. But before you use this, make sure there’s proper ventilation in the room to avoid getting suffocated from bleach vapors. Oxygen and bleach are good cleaning agents. They can effectively remove yellowish and dark stains on tiles and grouts.

You can buy commercial oxy-bleach products in stores for you to use on cleaning your tile floors. When applying this product, let them sit on your tiles for 10 to 15 minutes, so they can work more effectively.
